stem: A ticketing platform needs to offload heavy reporting reads from the writer and can accept asynchronous replica lag in report data.

choices.text: Create read replicas and route reporting queries to replica endpoints.
Use a Multi-AZ DB instance standby as the reporting query endpoint.
Increase writer instance class and keep all reports on the writer endpoint.
Restore the latest automated backup into a separate reporting instance.

rationale: Read replicas receive asynchronous updates from the writer and serve read traffic on their own endpoints, which is what offloading heavy reporting requires. A Multi-AZ DB instance standby is a failover target and does not serve read queries. Increasing the writer instance class adds capacity but leaves reporting contending with production writes on the same endpoint. Restoring an automated backup produces a point-in-time copy that is stale the moment it comes up and has to be repeated, so it is not a continuous read offload.
